events.promise: A bounded test with one real offer lets the reader judge whether MarketingOS can turn their own material and request into a grounded, reviewed email draft worth taking further—while leaving facts, links and brand-voice approval with them.
events.arc: Email 1 moves from having an invited account to running the smallest useful test: one real offer and one requested email. Email 2 moves from receiving a plausible-looking draft to evaluating it systematically through its source facts and cold-reader feedback, then recording what should stay, change or be corrected.

emails.job: Get the invited tester to run the smallest useful MarketingOS test with one real SaaS offer.
emails.single_idea: Do not begin with a full campaign: sign in, supply the real offer material, and request one launch or onboarding email so MarketingOS can be judged on a concrete draft rather than a product description.
emails.objection: A pilot run could consume more attention than it is worth, and a generation can take several minutes. Answer by bounding the test to one real offer and one email, without promising that it will be faster than writing.
must_not_say: Do not ask the reader to register, request access, book a demo or start a public trial; the account already exists and public registration is closed.
Do not claim the draft will save time, outperform their current method, be ready to send unchanged or produce opens, clicks, conversions or revenue.
Do not assume what writing or sending tools they use, how large their list or team is, what results they get, or how urgent the campaign is.
Do not introduce competitor analysis, audience research, contact finding, LinkedIn work or the full campaign pipeline; this email owns only the one-email first test.
Do not mention a price, discount, free tier, trial period, testimonial or customer result.
Do not reuse claims from the older orqAgent agent-builder product, including agents, Slack bots, integrations or credits.
emails.felt_need: They need launch or onboarding email copy for a real SaaS offer and want to know whether this pilot account can produce something usable.
emails.mechanism: The reader can point MarketingOS at a website or upload a PDF or screenshot, describe the needed email in their own words, and make the first run deliberately narrow: one real offer and one email. Disclose that generation can take several minutes rather than presenting it as instant.
emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS account, add the website, PDF or screenshot for one real offer, and request one launch or onboarding email: https://app.orqagent.com/login/
emails.next_step_decision: Whether the first draft is relevant and grounded enough to merit a fuller review or another campaign request.
emails.next_step_value: The existing-account sign-in leads to the workspace where the reader can supply real offer material and request one email in their own words.
emails.next_step_limit: This tests one requested email only; it does not establish full-sequence quality, sector-wide reliability or campaign performance.

emails.job: Get the tester to inspect the run methodically and record useful pilot feedback on the draft.
emails.single_idea: A draft should not be judged only by whether it sounds polished: inspecting the facts behind its claims and the cold-reader feedback reveals what is grounded, what an outsider understood, and what still needs correction.
emails.objection: A reviewed draft can still contain a factual error or wording the tester would replace. Answer by presenting source facts and cold-reader feedback as inspection aids, not as guarantees or substitutes for their judgment.
must_not_say: Do not claim that compiled facts eliminate factual errors or that cold-reader review guarantees clarity, quality or commercial performance.
Do not imply that MarketingOS sends or publishes the email, or that the tester can skip checking facts, links and brand voice.
Do not invent a particular audit dashboard, reviewer transcript or interface beyond the source facts and reader feedback the tester is being asked to inspect.
Do not broaden the email into competitor research, audience research, contact finding or LinkedIn messaging.
Do not imply that a positive review settles price, continued access, subscription terms or suitability for every SaaS business.
Do not mention testimonials, performance gains, public signup or claims from the older orqAgent agent-builder product.
emails.felt_need: They need a reliable way to decide which parts of the generated email they would keep, rewrite or reject before using it.
emails.status_quo: The pilot leaves the final judgment with the tester, who must decide whether the draft's claims and wording are suitable for the real offer.
emails.mechanism: MarketingOS first compiles supplied material into facts it is allowed to claim, then has the draft read by someone without product knowledge and rewrites what did not land. Ask the tester to inspect those two layers: compare claims with the source facts, then use the reader feedback to identify unclear language. Record phrases to keep or rewrite, factual errors and editing time; do not imply that this removes the tester's final review.
emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS account, open the run for one real offer, and review its source facts, reader feedback and draft: https://app.orqagent.com/login/
emails.next_step_decision: Which phrases are worth keeping, which need rewriting, whether any claims are wrong, and whether the draft merits further use.
emails.next_step_value: Inside the existing account, the tester can generate or reopen a reviewed draft and assess it against the pilot's requested feedback: phrases to keep or rewrite, factual errors and editing time.
emails.next_step_limit: The inspection does not prove opens, clicks, revenue or conversions, and it does not remove the tester's responsibility to check facts, links and brand voice before transferring the text.

events.subject: Review facts and reader feedback
events.preview_text: Separate factual grounding from what an unfamiliar reader understood.
events.body:
MarketingOS is an email campaign drafting and market-research application that lets you inspect a draft in two layers: what its claims are based on, and what an unfamiliar reader understood.

First, compare each claim with the source facts compiled from your offer material. Those facts constrain what the draft is allowed to claim, but they do not replace your check of the facts, links and brand voice.

Then read the feedback from someone without product knowledge. MarketingOS uses that outside reading to rewrite what did not land; the feedback helps you identify language that may still be unclear rather than treating a fluent draft as finished.

In your existing account, open the run for one real offer and review its source facts, reader feedback and draft. Note the phrases you would keep or rewrite, any factual errors, and the time you spend editing.

events.subject: What the draft still leaves unclear
events.preview_text: Separate factual grounding from what an unfamiliar reader understood.
events.body:
A line-by-line read can tell you whether an email sounds polished. It still leaves you to trace each claim to the offer material and work out what an unfamiliar reader actually understood.

MarketingOS is an email campaign drafting and market-research application. It compiles supplied material into allowed facts, has the email read by someone without product knowledge, and rewrites what did not land.

Those layers are inspection aids, not a guarantee. Compare the draft’s claims with the source facts, then use the reader feedback to find language that remains unclear; check facts, links and brand voice before using the copy.

Inside your existing account, you can reopen the run and assess its facts, feedback and draft together. Note the phrases worth keeping or rewriting, any factual errors and the time spent editing—so grounding and comprehension are judged separately.

edits.line: MarketingOS is an email campaign drafting and market-research application that lets you inspect a draft in two layers: what its claims are based on, and what an unfamiliar reader understood.
edits.problem: The central offer turns an evidenced internal drafting process into an unsupported user-visible inspection capability.
edits.fix: Do not promise access to these two layers unless product material confirms that they are exposed in the account; otherwise base the proposition on the supported reviewed draft the user can assess and transfer.

edits.line: First, compare each claim with the source facts compiled from your offer material.
edits.problem: This instruction assumes the tester can view the compiled facts, which none of the supplied product evidence establishes.
edits.fix: Remove the instruction unless evidence confirms that source facts are visible, or limit the task to checking the delivered draft against the tester's own offer material.

edits.line: Then read the feedback from someone without product knowledge. MarketingOS uses that outside reading to rewrite what did not land; the feedback helps you identify language that may still be unclear rather than treating a fluent draft as finished.
edits.problem: The internal outside-reader review and rewrite are supported, but the claim that the tester can read that feedback is not.
edits.fix: Preserve the supported review-and-rewrite mechanism while avoiding any instruction to inspect reader feedback until its user-facing availability is documented.

edits.line: In your existing account, open the run for one real offer and review its source facts, reader feedback and draft.
edits.problem: Besides relying on the unsupported inspection surfaces, this presumes that a completed run already exists for every recipient, although only account access is established.
edits.fix: Make the next step conditional on an existing run or describe the supported generation step before review, without inventing a prepared result or a review duration.
